plan.goal: Exhaustively explore and critique the UX of the GitHub 404 page clone, focusing on interactive elements, visual fidelity, and responsive layout.
plan.summary: The run will sequentially validate all functional areas of the single-page 404 clone. It will begin with top navigation and footer links, proceed to test the central search mechanism and adjacent category buttons, and conclude with a mobile viewport evaluation to address identified tap-target warnings.
assumptions: Most navigation and footer links are placeholders pointing to '#'.
The search functionality may not perform a real search but might trigger fake suggestions or UI state changes.
risk_hotspots: Empty accessibility label on the primary GitHub logo link (ux-1).
Search input (ux-5) and Search button (ux-6) interaction and potential JS-driven fake suggestions.
Widespread small tap targets across top nav, category buttons, and footer links.

phases.title: Navigation and Layout Validation
phases.objective: Verify the functionality of top navigation and footer links, and check the structural layout.
key_checks: Click the unlabelled logo link (ux-1) to see where it routes.
Click 'Search' (ux-2), 'Support' (ux-3), and 'Status' (ux-4) in the top nav.
Verify the 'contact support' (ux-10) and 'GitHub Status' (ux-11) links at the bottom.
exit_criteria: All header and footer links have been interacted with and their destination or lack thereof is confirmed.

phases.title: Search Mechanism Testing
phases.objective: Test the central search input and its submission.
key_checks: Type a test query into 'Search GitHub' (ux-5) and observe if any fake search suggestions appear.
Click the green 'Search' button (ux-6) and check if it submits a form or alters the URL.
Press 'Enter' while focused on the search input.
exit_criteria: Search input accepts text, and form submission behavior is documented.

phases.title: Category Buttons Interaction
phases.objective: Validate the behavior of the buttons located below the search bar.
exit_criteria: All three category buttons have been clicked to see if they act as filters, links, or visual toggles.

phases.title: Mobile Viewport Assessment
phases.objective: Evaluate the page layout and usability on a mobile viewport, focusing on the small tap target layout warnings.
key_checks: Assess if the top navigation collapses into a hamburger menu or if it cramps the screen.
Re-evaluate the interactability of the category buttons (ux-7, ux-8, ux-9) and footer links.
exit_criteria: Mobile viewport screenshot captured and layout structure analyzed for usability issues.

coverage_targets.features: Exercise all navigation links, the search input, submit button, and category filters.
coverage_targets.mobile: Switch to mobile viewport to specifically test the layout of the flagged small tap targets.

notes: The readme mentions a parallax/hover effect on the illustration; note any visual changes during mouse movements or interactions if the framework captures them.
